data.note: buglane31: standing approval window never reopens after lapse

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `if r["policy"] and r["answered_at"] and r["verb"] in cfg.approvals.standing_verbs and (r["policy"] or r["opened_window"])` uses `r["policy"]` redundantly on both sides of the `and`, rendering `r["opened_window"]` completely unreachable because `r["policy"]` evaluates to `True` for policy fires and `False` for operator answers that set `opened_window=True`. Given a logged answer where `r["policy"]` is `False` and `r["opened_window"]` is `True`, the expression `r["policy"] and ...` evaluates to `False`, so operator re-opens are never included in `starts` and lapsed windows are never re-opened.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s name and docstring say it checks that the window reopens only when the answer actually names a repository, but the negative case does not construct a “window answer with no repository path.” It answers the lapsed ask with `window=False`, i.e. a plain approve that never requests a window at all. If the fixed policy code re-anchors `window_start` whenever `window=True` regardless of whether a repository is present, this test still passes because it never exercises `window=True` without a repo, so the stated repo-scoping condition is untested and the test gives false assurance.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_policy.py:test_the_window_choice_only_reopens_when_it_names_a_repo

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s name and docstring say it checks that the window reopens only when the answer actually names a repository, but the negative case does not construct a “window answer with no repository path.” It answers the lapsed ask with `window=False`, i.e. a plain approve that never requests a window at all. If the fixed policy code re-anchors `window_start` whenever `window=True` regardless of whether a repository is present, this test still passes because it never exercises `window=True` without a repo, so the stated repo-scoping condition is untested and the test gives false assurance.

Given a logged answer where `r["policy"]` is `False` and `r["opened_window"]` is `True`, the expression `r["policy"] and ...` evaluates to `False`, so operator re-opens are never included in `starts` and lapsed windows are never re-opened.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes only the test name and docstring, leaving the test body unchanged from the prior `test_the_window_choice_only_reopens_when_it_names_a_repo`, which by its old docstring exercised the no-repository-path window-choice case. The new docstring claims this test verifies that a plain `window=False` approval never re-anchors the standing window, but because the body was not edited to perform that plain-approve scenario and assert on `policy.window_start`, the test can still pass even if plain approvals are changed to update the window anchor. In that case the B6e5e17ccda regression test would not fail on the unfixed/regressed behavior; it would continue to test the old no-repo window-choice path while advertising the plain-approve path.
